A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Plasticity-Ceiling study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original SFT/RL experiments on Qwen2.5 and Llama3.2, including training curves, benchmark performance and fitted performance ceilings.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds out-of-domain evaluations, another comparator, larger-model validation and supplementary data analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed ceiling-estimation model gains a fitted nonnegative alignment offset in v2 Equation 2, whereas v1 Equation 12 anchors the curve directly at the SFT performance. This extends the estimation method; the underlying SFT and RL training objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds GPQA-Diamond, with 198 prompts, and ARC-C, with 1,172 prompts, to evaluate transfer beyond the mathematical benchmarks retained from v1. This substantially expands evaluation coverage into science and out-of-domain reasoning.

E2.justification: Prefix-RFT becomes an evaluated comparator in Figure 2, extending v1's synchronized-method comparison of LUFFY, SRFT and UPT. The established comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix H adds protocols using Qwen2.5-14B and 55K training examples, intermediate 220K/440K sample sizes, and a full-SFT889K paradigm comparison with batch size 64, a 12,000-token response limit and 400 RL steps. The reported curve-fitting training/validation split also changes from approximately 85/15 to an average of 71/29.

E4.justification: v2 adds OOD transition-timing curves, paradigm robustness checks on SFT889K, intermediate-scale sensitivity experiments and a 14B-model transition study. Appendix G.1 additionally validates the difficulty proxy through logical-step analysis and human checks, substantially expanding tests of generality and mechanism.

E5.justification: Statistical estimation changes within the retained robust-fitting approach: Table 4 changes which runs use least-trimmed-squares fitting and introduces trimming fractions of 0.75 alongside 0.85. Appendix F also specifies an observed-peak fallback for unstable runs. Neither version reports independent training-seed replication or uncertainty intervals for the principal performance estimates.

E6.justification: Many central results change: Figure 3 revises the maximum SFT889K ceiling from 85.7 to 84.0, and Table 1 revises Llama3.2-3B SFT889K-to-DAPOdc performance from 70.1 to 70.4. v2 also adds Prefix-RFT, OOD, intermediate-scale and 14B results. Revised fitting and incompletely documented scoring history limit interpretation of these revisions as direct performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 2 changes the mathematical scaling model by introducing an alignment offset between the SFT endpoint and fitted RL trajectory. The central plasticity identity and numerical definitions of the SFT regimes are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The three principal recommendations remain: sequential training, transitioning near SFT saturation, and prioritizing data scale with difficulty as a secondary factor. v2 explicitly narrows the principal scope to mathematical reasoning and extends the transition-timing claim to OOD performance.

C2.justification: v1 attributes harder data's advantage to both stronger SFT performance and greater RL plasticity; v2 instead describes stronger SFT performance with comparable plasticity. v2 also adds explanations linking initialization to OOD findings and SFT compute to exploration, plus explicit limitations concerning mathematical tasks and R1-style trajectories.

D1.justification: v2 adds detailed evaluation procedures, strict/lenient grading and LLM adjudication, judge settings and audits, exact Llama checkpoint selections, per-fit outlier thresholds, and prompts/examples in Tables 7–9. These substantially improve documentation. The newly disclosed in-domain grading procedure does not by itself establish that grading changed from v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Prefix-RFT, ARC/GPQA, the DeepSeek evaluators, OOD generalization and entropy-preserving SFT. It also positions its OOD findings against prior work through an initialization-based explanation, while retaining the main research positioning around expert trajectory utilization.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: v1's detailed algorithmic preliminaries move to Appendix B and are replaced by a concise main-text summary. The framework and Llama discussions are rewritten, appendices are reorganized and expanded, and limitations are added.

P2.justification: v2 switches to a two-column layout, adds Figures 4, 6 and 7 and Tables 5–9, and expands Tables 3 and 4 with additional columns. Existing plots receive revised annotations and axes; v1 Figures 4 and 5 are retained as v2 Figures 5 and 8.

improvement.justification: The added OOD, intermediate-scale and 14B checks strengthen support for the recommendations, while evaluation details and explicit limitations improve reproducibility and scope. These gains are tempered by new numerical inconsistencies: v2 Table 4 gives the Pure-RL ceiling as 77.3, although Figure 3 and its components give 46.7 + 25.3 = 72.0; Section 6.3 reports 70.4 at 532.5 exaFLOPs while Figure 5 plots 71.4. These defects limit confidence in precise quantitative conclusions.
